question: Which hormonal event triggers Lactogenesis II (onset of copious milk secretion)?

answers.text: Surge in prolactin due to the suckling reflex on day 2

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Prolactin rises with suckling, but it is not the trigger for Lactogenesis II — it was already elevated during pregnancy without causing secretion.
Correct. High placental progesterone suppresses milk secretion despite adequate prolactin. Delivery of the placenta removes this block, initiating Lactogenesis II (milk 'coming in') around day 2–3.

answers.text: Rise in oestrogen produced by the involuting uterus

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Oestrogen promotes mammary gland development during pregnancy but does not trigger milk secretion — it actually inhibits lactation at high levels.

answers.text: Increase in oxytocin released by infant suckling

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Oxytocin drives milk ejection (let-down reflex), not the onset of milk synthesis. These are distinct physiological events.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review Lactogenesis stages: progesterone from the placenta suppresses secretion during pregnancy; its removal at delivery is the key trigger.
Well done. Placental progesterone withdrawal is the gate that opens Lactogenesis II — this explains why retained placental fragments delay milk coming in.
